preamble: Each across solution has a common definition, which is missing from its clue.

clue.text: Revolutionary soldiers in repeated word calling attention to emperor

indicators.note: in puts the turned soldiers inside the doubled greeting
repeated asks for the attention-calling word to be written down twice in a row

parts.note: 'Hi!' is a word used to call someone's attention

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Mutinous troops shout a repeated cry to get the emperor's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hi!' is the word for calling attention, so 'repeated' doubles it; 'Revolutionary' and 'in' do the rest, and the final word is taken as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirohito was the Japanese emperor from 1926 to 1989, a specific example of the title.

clue.text: There's nothing good about villain

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O
RE is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Nothing good can be said about a wicked character.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale monster that terrorises others serves as a villain in stories.

clue.text: Modern miss in upsetting experience — so one in distress?

indicators.note: in puts the title inside the turned word
in a down clue upsetting turns a word upside down, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: to lead a life of hardship is to experience it, so lead stands for experience
Ms is the modern title for a woman, married or not

explanation.surface: A modern young woman in a nasty experience, so is she a maiden in peril?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reads the experience word upwards and 'in' houses the modern title. The question mark flags a definition by example: the stock figure is the damsel in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale maiden needing rescue is proverbially described as being in distress.

clue.text: One's present PM's bringing in end for the Left

indicators.note: bringing in, with for, signals that one piece replaces another inside the Prime Minister's name

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attending as the Prime Minister brings in an end to the Left's policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in end for the Left' swaps the L of ATTLEE for END, giving ATTENDEE. Attlee led a Labour (left-wing) government, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends an event is present at it, so 'one present' describes them.

clue.text: Maybe watch someone unimportant

definitions.meaning: a watch is a ..., read literally as two words
a minor figure of no great consequence, especially in crime or business

explanation.definitionFit: A small-time operator is a minor, unimportant figure, and a watch is a little timing device.

clue.text: There's a place in Middlesex for bowler but not opener

indicators.note: but not opener means the bowler's word loses its first letter

parts.note: a spinner is a bowler of spin in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket club in Middlesex has a bowler but no opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not opener' drops the S from SPINNER. Middlesex is a historic English county now largely within north-west London; 'opener' also suggests an opening batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinner is a suburb of north-west London, historically part of the county of Middlesex.

clue.text: Trailing badly

indicators.note: badly tells us the letters of the word trailing are put in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Lagging behind badly in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TRAILING. The missing definition is 'bird': a ringtail is a female or young hen harrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringtail is a name for the female hen harrier, a bird of prey, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Fun to be had around a new town

indicators.note: around puts the word for fun on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a prank

explanation.surface: Fun is to be had around a newly built town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps LARK round A and N. Lanark is a market town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a historic market town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Time to forget about time

parts.note: T again stands for time

indicators.note: about puts the omitting word round the second time

parts.note: to omit something is to forget or leave it out
T again stands for time

explanation.surface: It is time to forget all about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places T inside OMIT, giving OMTIT, after the first T. The missing definition is 'bird': a tomtit is a small tit, especially a blue tit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomtit is a popular name for a small titmouse, a common garden bird.

clue.text: Port running short

indicators.note: running short means the port's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Dover is the Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A harbour town running low on supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' cuts the R from DOVER. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove is a familiar bird of the pigeon family, an example of the missing class.

clue.text: Smoother fish

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A tool for smoothing and a fish, listed side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing definition is 'bird': the sanderling is a small wading bird seen on beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanderling is a small sandpiper that runs along the tideline, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Slithers badly with pulpy stuff around

indicators.note: around puts the pulp word on the outside of the jumbled letters

parts.note: mush is soft pulpy matter

indicators.note: badly says the letters of slithers are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Something slides clumsily through a pulpy mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the printed word and 'around' wraps the pulp round it. The missing definition is 'bird'; the missel or mistle thrush feeds on mistletoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The missel thrush, or mistle thrush, is a large European thrush that eats mistletoe berries.

clue.text: Irish politicians always imbibing booze? That's an inhuman complaint

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the party abbreviation takes the booze inside it

parts.note: SF is Sinn Féin, the Irish political party
wine is a kind of booze
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Irish politicians forever drinking: is that a beastly ailment?
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' has the party drink the booze. 'Inhuman' here means affecting animals rather than people, not cruel; Sinn Féin is an Irish republican party.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine fever is a disease of pigs, so it is a complaint suffered by animals rather than humans.

clue.text: Maybe claret's acidic

parts.note: claret is an example of a red wine, so claret's gives red's
tart means sharp or acidic in taste

explanation.surface: Perhaps this claret is rather sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that claret is just one example of a red. The missing definition is 'bird': the redstart is a small songbird with a red tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird of the thrush family with a rust-coloured tail.

clue.text: An 'orrible place outside port

indicators.note: outside puts the dropped-h place round the port's name

parts.note: 'orrible drops its h, so the place meant is a hole, said without its h
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Somewhere 'orrible, said in a Cockney accent, just beyond the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'orrible tells you to drop the H of the place too, mimicking a Cockney accent; 'outside' then wraps it round the port. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriole is a brightly coloured songbird, the golden oriole being the European species.

clue.text: John noticed agenda's fifth item: Unfinished business

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
seen means noticed

indicators.note: fifth item picks the fifth letter of the word agenda

explanation.surface: John noticed the fifth item on the agenda, still unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is a slang toilet here, not a man. The fifth letter of AGENDA is D.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail left unresolved, an idiom for unfinished business.

clue.text: Join with partners at card table

parts.note: a seam is a join between pieces of material
East and West are partners at bridge, abbreviated E and W

explanation.surface: Sitting together with your partner at a bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are North, South, East and West, with North-South and East-West as partnerships. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea mew is an old name for the common gull, a seabird.

clue.text: We'll need women in smart TV show

parts.note: the word we is taken from we'll

indicators.note: in puts the women's letter inside the word for smart

parts.note: to smart is to sting, as a wound does

explanation.surface: We will need some women in a stylish television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the women inside the smart word. 'Smart' is a verb meaning hurt, not 'stylish'. The West Wing is an American political drama series.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Wing is an American political drama set in the White House, so it is a TV show.

clue.text: Girl brought on board to get fish

indicators.note: brought on board means taken inside the ship, so the girl's name goes within SS

parts.note: board here means a ship, so SS, steamship, stands for it
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl brings her catch of fish on board the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention for going inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates are flat cartilaginous fish related to rays, so they are a kind of fish.

clue.text: Bathe by coastal hazard?

parts.note: lave is a literary word meaning to bathe or wash
a rock is a danger to ships near the coast

explanation.surface: Is it safe to take a dip near a dangerous shoreline?
explanation.walkthrough: The missing definition is 'bird': laverock is an old Scots and Northern word for the skylark.
explanation.definitionFit: Laverock is a dialect name for the skylark, a songbird.

clue.text: Lord upset over rising wickedness

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the fuss above the next piece

parts.note: an ado is a fuss or upset

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A nobleman is upset by mounting immorality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SIN into NIS. The definition is fair because the name Adonis comes from the Semitic word adon, meaning lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The god's name derives from the Phoenician and Hebrew adon, a title meaning master or lord.

clue.text: See 12
Ball goes into river somewhere by the sea

indicators.note: goes into puts the sphere word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A ball rolls into a river at a seaside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Torbay is a coastal borough in Devon, England, known as the English Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Torbay is a resort area on the south Devon coast, so it lies beside the sea.

clue.text: Another broadcast to draw in viewer

indicators.note: to draw in means the jumbled letters take the viewer inside them
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of another are spread out of order

parts.note: an eye is the organ that views

explanation.surface: Another programme is broadcast to attract more viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles the printed word into HONATER, and 'to draw in' splits it to take the viewer in the middle. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeyeaters are an Australasian family of songbirds that feed on nectar.

clue.text: Loud hooter

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
an owl hoots, so it is a hooter

explanation.surface: A noisy car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn or a nose, but here it is the bird that hoots. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl is a general word for a bird, especially domestic poultry.

clue.text: Church congregation to go bust

definitions.meaning: the faithful of a church, as a flock in a sheep pen
to collapse or close down, as a failing business does

explanation.definitionFit: A fold is a church's flock of believers, and a business that collapses is said to fold.

clue.text: Holy dope with nothing to hide

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning holy

indicators.note: to hide means the dope word conceals the zero inside it

parts.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope
nothing is zero, written as O

explanation.surface: A saintly fool with nothing to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' means inside information, not a fool or drug. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common stout-bodied bird of the dove family.

clue.text: Brief love affair making female celebrity

indicators.note: making signals that the female letter is turned into another piece within the affair word

parts.note: a fling is a short romantic affair
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A short romance turns an ordinary woman into a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making female celebrity' turns the F of FLING into STAR. The missing definition is 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird with glossy speckled plumage, known for flocking.
